For N=2, the sole nonconstant mode has s_1=1; at nu=1/sqrt(2) its roots are ±i, while at nu=1 the polynomial is (r+1)^2.

entry.asserts: For N=2, the only nonconstant mode has z=-1 and S=0: centered amplification is 1 and Lax–Friedrichs has modulus 1 for every nu.

entry.asserts: For N=2 and the Nyquist mode, s_1=1. At nu=1 the polynomial is (r+1)^2 and the modified energy of (Y,X)=(-X,X) is zero; at nu=2 its roots are -7±4sqrt(3), one has modulus greater than one, and that energy is -6||X||^2/k^2.
entry.claim: The endpoint repeated root and strict super-CFL growth already occur on the smallest even periodic grid.

entry.asserts: With N=4, z=i and nu=1/2, g_up=(1-i)/2 has squared modulus 1/2 and g_down=(3-i)/2 has squared modulus 5/2.
entry.claim: The same finite Fourier mode decays for upwind and grows for downwind.

entry.asserts: With N=4, z=i and nu=1/2, g_centered=1-i/2 and |g_centered|^2=5/4>1 while 0<nu<1.
entry.claim: The centered stencil is power-unstable despite the strict upwind CFL range.

entry.asserts: For N=4, z=i and nu=1/2, one upwind Fourier mode has factor (1-i)/2 with squared modulus 1/2. This verifies the per-grid contraction example and supplies no fixed Banach-space lift.
entry.claim: A finite grid power bound coexists with the absent common-space interface premise.
